summary: In this story, a boy forgets his homework on the way to school and learns that staying calm, telling the truth, and making a real plan matter more than making an excuse.
introduce: Act out a short mime, such as checking your watch and tapping your foot, and ask students how you feel and how they know. Explain that in “The Lost Homework” they will use clues in the same way to work out what the writer does not say directly.

keyTerms.def: able to be trusted to do the right thing
to say that something is true, especially something you did wrong
a result that happens because of something you did

challengeTerms.def: the quality of doing the right thing, even when no one is watching
responsible for your own actions and ready to answer for them
done on purpose, after careful thought

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that if you forget your homework, it is better to make a good excuse than to admit you forgot? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Yusuf shows responsibility after he realizes he forgot his homework.
struggling: Pre-teach responsible, admit, and consequence with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses integrity, accountable, and deliberate to make an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
